chapter: Alice Zeno: languages and the King household
title: Language classes at the King house and Miss Gracie's advice
summary: Alice describes the daily French, Spanish and German conversation classes in the household and how she learned to take the opportunity seriously.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You told me about the people, this lady that you worked for at Tulane or Newcomb College. One time she found you reading some books she didn't like.
Oh, was that who it was? I thought it was the other people.
No, no. That was Mrs. King. Oh.
And you read how many languages? Un peu.
Comme ci, comme ça. I understand pretty good. And in French?

In French. In French. Well, you see, when I was working at Mrs. King, they had...it wasn't a school. It was just like you're nice, convoicing you. Yes. They had Mr. Chaffray. You must have heard of that name, Chaffray? I'm not sure.

And then they had Mrs. Lodoux and Mrs. C.J. Sam's and all. And they speak. Well, that day, that day, that day was just like conversion, it was as if it was French. They had an old lady they called Madame Gérard. She was French. And Charles Gaiary.
Oh, yes. He's a famous man, a historian.

Well, it was nothing but French. And then the next day, it was maybe the Spanish class. Well, that was Capitano Chivarillo. Nothing but Spanish. Nothing. They speak to me in Spanish, the language of the class that was going on. And Herman Gessner. Herman Gessner teaches. That must be his grandson that is teaching at Tulane. Yes, I've heard that name. Yes, Herman Gessner. Well, then him, he was Spanish, German. And nothing but German. They called me and they speak to me in German and asked me things in German. No other language but the language of that day.
So you had to learn all of those languages too?

Well, you know, young, I was young and foolish at last. And one day, Miss Gracie told me, Harps is fee. You have an opportunity of learning things that you will never be able to pay for. And you're there giggling and giggling. And after a while, I said, well, I think Miss Gracie is right. Let me stop giggling and pay attention to what... What I...the opportunity that I had. So there's where I began to catch on. A little German. A little Spanish. Well, I knew French well.
